title: The Our Father
subtitle: Line-by-Line Breakdown of the Lord's Prayer

sections.content: When asked by His disciples how to pray, Jesus taught them the Our Father (Matthew 6:9-13). Saint Augustine called it the perfect prayer because it contains every valid petition human beings can offer to God.

items: **'Our Father, who art in heaven'** — Establishes our relationship as adopted sons and daughters of God.
**'Hallowed be Thy name'** — A prayer that God's holiness be recognized and revered across the earth.
**'Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven'** — Submitting our desires to the holy, sovereign will of God.
**'Give us this day our daily bread'** — Asking for both temporal nourishment and the Spiritual Bread of the Eucharist.
**'And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us'** — Conditioning our reception of God's mercy on our willingness to forgive others.
**'And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil'** — Seeking divine protection from Satan and spiritual ruin.

sections.title: Key Takeaway
sections.content: The first three petitions focus on God's glory; the final four address our human needs and vulnerabilities.
